The second term hit, late and ill-guided, left Aliir concussed and puts van Rooyen in danger of missing a final.

With Port Adelaide’s season over for several weeks now, Melbourne wasted no time in getting to work and had established a 36-point lead by quarter time.

Port’s willingness to kick long and high worked quite literally worked straight into the hands of the Demon defenders, who intercepted and propelled time after time. Melbourne was far more efficient having scored nine times from their first 11 inside-50s.

report.headline: Giants power past Eagles to remain alive in wildcard hunt
report.text:
Greater Western Sydney keeps its faint wildcard hopes alive with a commanding performance against West Coast

Needing a win to maintain their slim hopes of a wild card spot, the Giants kicked nine straight goals as they charged to a 16.15 (111) to 7.15 (57) victory at Engie Stadium on Sunday.

To snare a spot in the finals, the Giants need Carlton to lose on Sunday afternoon against the Western Bulldogs and in the final round, while the Giants also need to beat Adelaide next week.

They turned a 16-point first-quarter deficit into 35 and 47-point leads at half and three-quarter time.

West Coast slumped to a 10th straight loss despite winning the clearances and racking up the same number of inside 50s.

Their lack of accuracy across the two middle quarters proved costly with the Giants kicking 8.5 to the Eagles' 0.9.

report.headline: They're in! Blues' EPIC draw with Dogs secures finals, season over for Saints, Giants
report.text:
Carlton and the Western Bulldogs draw to secure the Blues a spot in finals

Under the guidance of interim coach Josh Fraser, the Blues have confirmed a wildcard position with a round to play, following a dramatic draw with the Western Bulldogs on Sunday afternoon.

Captain Patrick Cripps put the side on his back, leading the 12.10 (82) stalemate under the Marvel Stadium roof, as he finished with 33 disposals and 12 clearances out of the middle.

His midfield proteges Sam Walsh (33 disposals, 318 metres gained) and Jagga Smith (25 disposals, six inside 50s) flanked him, pulling the Blues back up every time it looked as if the Bulldogs had landed the crucial blow.

In a see-sawing encounter at Marvel Stadium, the Blues trialled by seven points with six minutes remaining, with a Bulldogs win to leave Fraser's side needing to beat Fremantle next week to guarantee finals.

report.headline: Swans fend off gritty Bombers, lock in top two
report.text:
Essendon got within two goals before Sydney kicked away in the final term

The Swans dominated from the start and, despite some resistance from the Bombers, easily won 17.10 (112) to 11.10 (76) in the Sunday twilight game at the MCG.

Errol Gulden racked up a career-best 47 possessions, and Charlie Curnow kicked four goals as he closed in on his third Coleman Medal.

While the Bombers were never going to stage a massive upset, they scrapped hard after a blowout loomed early in the game.

report.headline: Suns spoil veteran's 300th with tough win over Saints
report.text:
Gold Coast might have been the side to close out the season with the four points thanks to the 14.19 (103) to 12.8 (80) scoreline against St Kilda at Marvel Stadium on Thursday evening, but in the context, it meant very little.

Skill errors littered the match, and frustrations showed themselves across the field as a result, with spotfires popping up everywhere and players punching the deck when turning the ball over.

Instead, focus was on 300-gamer Bradley Hill, becoming the ninth First Nations player to the milestone, and retirees Nick Holman and Dougal Howard.

report.headline: Morris mauls Pies with eight-goal bag as Lions all but lock in third spot
report.text:
Brisbane is in the box seat for a third-placed finish after defeating Collingwood by 63 points

The Lions controlled the game from the outset and never really looked threatened, powering to a massive 25.9 (159) to 15.6 (96) demolition win.

It was an ominous warning sign to the rest of the competition, reaffirming they're still one of the best in the business as they chase a historic premiership three-peat.

Key forward Logan Morris was outstanding, booting a career-high eight goals from 15 disposals and eight marks to become the first Lion to kick eight goals in a game at the MCG.

The 21-year-old has become one of the most dangerous forwards in the competition as he eyes a maiden All-Australian blazer, the star Lion is a nightmare matchup for opposition defenders given his unique mix of athleticism and marking ability.

report.headline: Blues storm into September with statement win against minor premier
report.text:
Francis Evans kicked five goals as Carlton defeated Fremantle by 37 points

The Blues signalled their finals intent in a commanding performance, overcoming an early four-goal deficit in the 18.11 (119) to 12.10 (82) win at Marvel Stadium on Saturday.

A blockbuster knockout clash with arch-rivals Collingwood could be next, depending on other results over the weekend.

Sam Walsh (31 disposals), Jagga Smith (31) and captain Patrick Cripps (24) were all at the forefront of the Blues' dominance in the engine room against a lacklustre Fremantle.

Marc Pittonet shone in the ruck, Francis Evans kicked a career-best five goals, and Brodie Kemp and Ben Ainsworth added three each.

report.headline: Brilliant Bulldogs set up wildcard clash with Pies, Demons forced to wait
report.text:
The Western Bulldogs won an absolute classic against Melbourne ahead of the finals

That is Melbourne's reality. The Demons woke up Saturday morning with all number of possibilities, most of them involving a week's rest. Hell, even top four and a double chance was on the agenda. But they'll get home Saturday night watching games unfold elsewhere, knowing full well a do-or-die wildcard game is now on their own radar.

The Western Bulldogs, Melbourne's opponents on Saturday evening, didn't have such possibilities. They were playing next week regardless. It might have been why they arrived at the MCG unburdened to secure a 21-point upset that turned the tables on the Dees' year, if not necessarily their own.

The Bulldogs, in all likelihood, did save themselves an interstate trip to South Australia next week as a reward for their 16.12 (108) to 12.15 (87) victory. An MCG bout with Collingwood now probably awaits, as opposed to a hostile Adelaide Oval clash against the Crows.

report.headline: Cats flex muscles against hapless Tigers to dodge wildcard final
report.text:
Geelong will finish inside the top six and earn a week off after thrashing Richmond at GMHBA Stadium

The Cats have earned a week off and could finish as high as fourth if Hawthorn loses to West Coast on Sunday night, following their comprehensive 57-point victory over Richmond at GMHBA Stadium.

The home side did most of the damage in the first half, streaking to a 49-point lead at the main break before cruising to victory, 20.13 (133) to 11.10 (76).

Bailey Smith was arguably best afield, finishing with a game-high 40 disposals, 827 metres gained and three goals, while Shaun Mannagh collected 33 disposals and three goals.

It was almost as though Geelong coach Chris Scott dropped his coaching board on the way into the ground and forgot where he had placed his magnets, with several key Cats lining up in unfamiliar positions in the opening term.

Star forward Cameron, who was playing his first game since injuring his AC joint in round 18, started off the half-back line before moving forward in the second half.

Mannagh spent a large portion of the game in the midfield where he added another string to his bow, while still managing to drift forward for his three goals, all of which came inside the first 35 minutes.

report.headline: Crows lock in top six with big win over Giants
report.text:
Taylor Walker kicked six in his farewell home and away game in Adelaide

The Crows avoided the wildcard finals after Walker and Izak Rankine (35 touches, four goals) starred in a 24.13 (157) to 15.11 (101) triumph on Saturday night.

Adelaide hold fifth spot overnight, but will slip to sixth should Hawthorn's expected win over lowly West Coast on Sunday eventuate.

Veteran forward Walker was playing his last home-and-away game for the Crows, after announcing his looming retirement.

report.headline: Power condemn Bombers to wooden spoon with thrilling win
report.text:
The Power have kicked two late goals to overcome the Bombers in a thriller

Emerging forward Nate Caddy's career-best six-goal haul wasn't enough for the Bombers in their 16.9 (105) to 14.11 (95) defeat to the Power in Sunday's dead rubber at Marvel Stadium.

The result left wooden spooner Essendon with a 2-21 record for the year, worse than even the 2016 'top-ups' season which generated three wins.

The Bombers also won only two games in the 1933 VFL campaign, though that was in a shorter 18-round home and away season.

report.headline: Emotional Swans turn turmoil into triumph with victory over Roos
report.text:
Sydney caps a tough week with a resounding 53-point win over North Melbourne

The Swans stood tall to hand North Melbourne a 53-point beating on Sunday evening, capping off a turbulent week off the field with a dominant 17.21 (123) to 10.10 (70) victory.

The win came after Sydney made five changes following season-ending club suspensions for Riley Bice, Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney, James Jordon and Chad Warner due to behavioural breaches. In their place, Harry Cunningham, James Rowbottom, Angus Sheldrick, Caiden Cleary and Tom Hanily were all recalled to the senior side.

That emotion translated directly onto the stat sheet, with the Swans dominating inside-50s 70–39 and smashing the Kangaroos in the clearances 48–31. Sydney's ruthless efficiency sealed the deal, as it converted a blistering 57.1 per cent of their entries compared to North Melbourne's 48.7 per cent.

report.headline: Hawks stroll past Eagles to lock in top-four finish and date with Dockers
report.text:
Hawthorn has secured fourth place on the ladder and will face Fremantle in a qualifying final

The Hawks were dominant and raced to a 47-point lead in the second quarter, but wet weather thwarted their efforts to make up the necessary percentage on third-placed Brisbane, eventually winning 16.11 (107) to 6.9 (45).

The result was all but settled early in the third quarter, ensuring the Hawks finished in the top four for the first time since 2018 and celebrated spearhead Jack Gunston's 300th game in style, with the three-time premiership veteran bagging five goals.

There was late drama, however, with Nick Watson managed in the fourth quarter after a Mark of the Year contender and a late incident that saw him shoved into the boundary fence by Bo Allan.
